name: Generic desktop tower with a rear I/O panel
build: blender -b --factory-startup --python source/build_desktop_generic.py (builds the monitor and the tower), then glTF-Transform dedup → weld → meshopt
units: metres; origin at the centre of the base; FRONT faces +Z in three.js — the network port is on the BACK

anchors.port_eth: the network port, on the REAR panel (outward normal -Z; a scene that wants it facing a switch turns the tower)
anchors.led_link: link light, built into the jack (left)
anchors.led_act: activity light, built into the jack (right)
anchors.led_power: the power light on the front

rear: the network port with its two jack lights, as real motherboard ports have
the PSU plate with its fan grille and the mains inlet

behaviour: generic. The two lights are the ones on the jack itself: link (a working cable to a live partner) and activity (frames passing). A film checking 'the computer's link light' must go behind the machine — which is the point: that is where it is.

provenance.origin: original work, authored for OE by the explainer engine (procedural Blender script)
provenance.creator: OE Support explainer engine
provenance.license: OE-owned; no third-party geometry, textures or trademarks
